basis: Macroglossia, persistent hyperinsulinism and lateralized skeletal/soft-tissue overgrowth are cardinal BWS criteria. Tumour predisposition adds no organ.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: lateralized overgrowth involving skeletal muscle and bone is a cardinal Beckwith-Wiedemann diagnostic criterion.

basis: Microcephaly with primordial dwarfism/slender-bone skeletal disorder; restrictive cardiomyopathy and subglottic stenosis each occur in 1/2 patients. Frequency estimates are fragile.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the explicit primordial dwarfism/slender-bone disorder ancestry supports defining skeletal disease; metaphyseal sclerosis occurs in 1/2.

basis: Focal neurologic dystonia; structural mandibular and temporomandibular joint abnormalities are annotated in 30-79%. Dysphagia and dysphonia alone do not establish GI or airway damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: abnormal mandibular morphology and temporomandibular joint abnormalities in 30-79% support structural skeletal involvement beyond muscle spasms alone.

basis: Precursor B-cell leukemia/lymphoma occupies marrow; hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly 40-60%. CNS involvement is below 30%.

decisions.hepatic: involved: direct leukemic occupation of the liver with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly 40-60%; malignant infiltration qualifies without requiring hepatic failure.

basis: Cold-triggered autoinflammatory attacks cause transient rash and joint inflammation without established lasting injury. Hearing impairment occurs in only 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: despite arthritis annotated in 80-99%, typical FCAS joint inflammation is brief and resolves without established persistent joint damage.

basis: Neurodegeneration and photosensitive skin disease define ATLD2; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 4/4. Ocular telangiectasia and photophobia do not establish functional injury.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: photosensitive cutaneous disease with telangiectasia in 4/4 is a defining component of this DNA repair syndrome.

basis: CoA metabolic neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration/visual impairment 80-99%. Acanthocytosis lacks blood dysfunction; osteopenia can reflect immobility rather than direct skeletal disease.

decisions.haematologic: none: acanthocytosis is annotated in 30-79%, but abnormal red-cell morphology alone does not establish anemia, hemolysis or other blood dysfunction.

basis: Defining metabolic, cardiac and ocular syndrome; thrombocytopenia 30-79%. Corneal opacity 30-79%; hepatic storage/hepatomegaly 30-79% omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: primary: ophthalmoplegia is a named defining component, eye-disorder ancestry supports localization, and corneal opacity occurs in 30-79%.

basis: Adrenal cortisol excess directly causes myopathy/bone loss in roughly 50-80% and persistent skin atrophy/bruising in roughly 50-80%. Separately diagnosed hypertension is excluded.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension affects roughly 70-85% but is a separately diagnosed secondary condition; other direct cardiovascular injury is not established in at least 30%.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: cortisol directly causes persistent dermal atrophy, fragility and striae in roughly 50-80%; these represent structural skin damage.

basis: Nonsyndromic severe intellectual disability with microcephaly. Broad carbohydrate-transport ancestry does not establish a metabolic disorder; macroglossia lacks evidence of GI dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: the broad transport-disorder ancestor alone does not establish a metabolic disease in this nonsyndromic intellectual disability concept.
